facts.text: Singapore’s Central Area was defined as the commercial core in the 1950s Jackson Plan, shaping the city’s early skyline.
The 1991 Master Plan introduced regional centres to decentralise services, yet the Central Region remains the de facto regional centre for Singapore.
The Central Area’s grid layout supports the Mass Rapid Transit system, making it one of the most transit‑connected business districts in the world.
Singapore’s urban planning divides the island into 55 planning areas, with the Central Region hosting the busiest commercial hubs like Marina Bay and Raffles Place.
The Singapore Tourism Board, headquartered in the CBD, drives digital innovation in tourism, recently launching AI‑powered robodog guides for visitors.
Despite its small size, Singapore’s Central Area hosts the historic Merlion statue, a symbol that has become synonymous with the city’s identity.
